subject: Deferred remit schedule request — Solaris Health
messages:
From: Emma Jensen <emma.jensen@solarishq.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@solarishq.com
Date: Mon, 21 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Proposal and commercials for Redwood

Thanks, Monica — quick heads up from procurement: Solaris is asking for a deferred remit cadence for the first two quarters to align with our fiscal collections. Specifically, procurement is asking whether Redwood can accept quarterly invoicing in arrears or, alternately, net-90 for the first 90 days post-SOW.

We understand this is non-standard, but our board has pushed cashflow timing for vendor payments this year. If there is flexibility here (or a partial upfront payment structure), please let me know what would be required to move forward quickly — we need a commercial position to present to finance by EOD Wednesday.

Attached is Solaris' vendor intake form (procurement requested we share).

Best,
Emma Jensen
Head of Procurement | Solaris Health
emma.jensen@solarishq.com
+1 (415) 555-0123

Attachment: solaris_vendor_intake.pdf (form, 32KB)

From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
To: Emma Jensen <emma.jensen@solarishq.com>
Cc: aditya.rao@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 21 Jun 2027 09:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Proposal and commercials for Redwood

Emma — thanks for the flag and the intake form. We can be flexible but will need to protect startup economics on year-one deals. I've attached Proposal_v3 and the SOW that reflect the initial pricing. High-level options we can consider: 1) 30% deposit on signature + quarterly invoicing in arrears for the remainder; 2) 50% upfront then net-90 on remaining invoices; 3) standard net-30 with a small onboarding credit.

If Solaris is firm on quarterly or net-90, I need to escalate for finance / commercial approval and an exec sign-off given the ARR profile. Copying Aditya to confirm cadence and to propose a recommended path.

Goal: firm position to share back with procurement by EOD Wednesday.

Thanks,
Monica Patel
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
monica.patel@redwood.com | (650) 555-0199

Attachments: proposal_v3.pdf, SOW_solaris_v2.docx

From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Emma Jensen <emma.jensen@solarishq.com>
Cc: marcus.lin@redwood.com, lauren.bishop@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 21 Jun 2027 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Proposal and commercials for Redwood

Quick commercial take — for a strategic healthcare logo like Solaris we can make a one-quarter exception but with these guardrails: 1) 30% upfront at signature (non-refundable) to cover ramping costs; 2) quarterly billing in arrears after that, with final payment terms net-60 for each invoice; 3) no additional list-price discount beyond a standard PLG concession (we hold margin).

If finance prefers net-90 instead of net-60, we'll need either a higher upfront percentage (50%) or an exec-level credit approval given cashflow impact. Lauren / Marcus — requesting a quick thumbs here so Monica can respond to procurement.

Thanks,
Aditya Rao
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Cc: lauren.bishop@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 21 Jun 2027 11:32:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Proposal and commercials for Redwood

Monica / Aditya — I like the 30% deposit + quarterly in arrears with net-60 on subsequent invoices as a compromise. Two asks before I OK: 1) Finance sign-off on credit checks and PO cadence; 2) Contract clause for an automatic payment method conversion (ACH or CC on file) after the first quarter to reduce ongoing risk.

If finance can't accept net-60, we should require 50% upfront for net-90. Agree we should not give an additional price concession. Lauren, can you confirm cashflow impact and whether this needs an exec-level exception?

Marcus Lin
Head of Growth | Redwood Inference

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 22 Jun 2027 15:10:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Proposal and commercials for Redwood

Folks — reviewed with finance ops. We can accept net-60 with the following conditions: Solaris provides a valid PO before signature; we complete our standard credit check; Redwood retains the right to pause services if payment is >45 days late past invoice date. I've attached a draft payment_schedule.xlsx that models cashflow under the 30% deposit + quarterly in arrears approach.

Net-90 on the remainder is riskier. Finance will only accept net-90 if there is either (a) 50% upfront at signature, or (b) a CFO-level approval for the 30% deposit option (which would remain a one-off concession). If you want me to route for CFO approval, I need a one-paragraph business justification and expected ARR for year one.

Attachment: payment_schedule.xlsx (spreadsheet, 18KB)

Lauren Bishop
Sr. Finance Manager | Redwood Inference
lauren.bishop@redwood.com

From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 23 Jun 2027 09:00:00 -07:00
Subject: Exec approval request — Solaris deferred remit exception (one-off)

Markus — short summary and ask: Solaris Health (prospect) is requesting quarterly invoicing in arrears or net-90 for the first 90 days to match their internal collections. The commercial team recommends the following one-time exception if you approve: 1) 30% non-refundable deposit at signature; 2) quarterly invoicing in arrears thereafter, with net-60 payment terms on subsequent invoices; 3) contract clause to require PO before signature and automatic payment conversion (ACH/CC) after first quarter; 4) no additional price concession beyond standard PLG discount.

Why approve: Solaris is a prioritized healthcare pilot (potential ARR ~$420k in year one) and will provide valuable reference in the payer/provider space. We can mitigate risk with the deposit, PO and auto-pay conversion clause. Finance has indicated net-90 without 50% upfront would be unacceptable without CFO sign-off; the proposed compromise balances customer need and cash protection.

Requested decision: approve the one-off deferred remit arrangement under the terms above, or require the 50% upfront if you are not comfortable with 30% deposit + net-60. If you approve, I'll finalize the SOW and send the DocuSign link to Solaris today.

Links: HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/deals/12345 | DocuSign preview: https://www.docusign.com/pack/98765

Thanks,
Monica Patel
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
monica.patel@redwood.com | (650) 555-0199

Attachments: SOW_solaris_v2.docx, proposal_v3.pdf
